summary: One entry per version of each unit of the chart package (standard simai.linkage 1.0.0, journal-per-version). Renames and removals of a public name are change-journal records (simai.change-lifecycle), kept in the free journal's form in docs/chart/journal.json.

entries.summary: The chart core: data read from records or columns with a field mapping (a missing value is a gap), linear and calendar scales with round ticks, Intl number and date formats, line, step and monotone paths with gaps, min-max decimation past two points per pixel column, band scales, stacks (stacked and normalized, positive and negative apart, gaps kept), pie and donut slices, series facts for the summary, and the keyboard cursor. Not yet released, so the M1 additions stay in 0.1.0.

sf-chart-line, the first chart of the package: one or more series over time, a number or categories; axes, grid, a legend that hides series, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor said in a live region, a summary sentence, the same data as a table (toggle, visible, hidden), loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-sparkline: one series as a word-sized line, area or bars without axes, with a mark on the last value or the extremes; an image named by its label and a sentence of the data; loading and empty states.

sf-chart-bar: values by category as columns or horizontal bars, side by side, stacked or normalized to shares, sorted on request, with values at the bar ends; a value axis from zero, a legend that hides series, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor said in a live region, a summary sentence, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-pie: the parts of one whole as slices of a circle or a ring with the total in the middle, the smallest folded into «Другое» past max-parts; shares inside the slices, a legend with shares that hides parts (beside or under the plot by a container query), a tooltip, a keyboard cursor said in a live region, a summary sentence, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-metric: one number with its label in a number, currency or unit format; the change against a previous period with its meaning (better) said by tone, arrow and word; a limit as a meter with sf-progress-bar's look; the page's status with a hint; a chart slot for an sf-chart-sparkline; the whole tile as one link or button; loading and empty states.
bandPath: the band between an upper and a lower edge, per run, sharing their gaps; a stacked layer's smooth top is the same curve as the bottom of the layer on it.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do: bandPath is new, and areaPath and linePath draw as before.

entries.summary: stack: none, stacked (the series as layers, positive up and negative down from zero) or normalized (shares of the whole at each x on a 0–100 % axis, the cursor and the tooltip saying the share and the value); a layer always fills its band, keeps its gaps and shares its kept points with the other layers; the summary says the series are stacked.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do: stack defaults to none, so a chart without it draws as before; set stack to stack the series.

entries.summary: settled: the value a costly view shows for data that may change fast; a change after a quiet spell shows at once, a stream at most once per wait, the latest last.

The data table is rebuilt only when the data changes, never on a pointer or cursor move, and at most once per second while data streams; the first data shows at once. A line chart with table="hidden" updating 1,200 points went from 31 ms to 5 ms per update.

The data table is rebuilt only when the data changes, never on a pointer or cursor move, and at most once per second while data streams; the first data shows at once. A bar chart with table="hidden" updating 1,200 points went from 31 ms to 5 ms per update.

The data table is rebuilt only when the data changes, never on a pointer or cursor move, and at most once per second while data streams; the first data shows at once. A pie chart with table="hidden" updating 1,200 points went from 31 ms to 5 ms per update.

sf-chart-parts: the parts of one whole as one thin bar split into shares, with the free remainder of a capacity (max) named «Свободно»; the smallest folded into «Другое» past max-parts; the whole beside the label, a list of the parts with values and shares (or one inline line for a tile), a tooltip, a keyboard cursor said in a live region, a summary sentence, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

lines: series named in lines are drawn as lines with points over the bars (a plan over the facts), never stacked; line-axis own puts them on a scale of their own with its ticks on the far side (a margin over a revenue), always so over a normalized stack; line-format formats their values in the ticks, the tooltip, the live line and the table; the summary says which series are lines; the cursor walks onto a line and select carries it. Vertical bars only.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do: lines defaults to empty, so a chart without it draws as before; name series in lines to draw them as lines.

entries.summary: colors: a page's own colour per series, by its key, a Framework role (which follows the theme) or a CSS colour; a value that is not a colour is dropped and one under 3:1 against the background is reported in the console; a series without one keeps the palette by its place, and forced colours are unchanged.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do: colors defaults to empty, so a chart draws as before; give it {key: colour} to colour a series of your own.

entries.summary: colors: a page's own colour per series, by its key, a Framework role (which follows the theme) or a CSS colour; a value that is not a colour is dropped and one under 3:1 against the background is reported in the console; a series without one keeps the palette by its place, and forced colours are unchanged.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do: colors defaults to empty, so a chart draws as before; give it {key: colour} to colour a series of your own.

entries.consumer: Nothing to do: colors defaults to empty, so a chart draws as before; give it {key: colour} to colour a part of your own.

entries.summary: colors: a page's own colour per part, by its category, a Framework role (which follows the theme) or a CSS colour; a value that is not a colour is dropped and one under 3:1 against the background is reported in the console; a part without one keeps the palette by its place, and forced colours are unchanged.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do: colors defaults to empty, so a chart draws as before; give it {key: colour} to colour a part of your own.

entries.summary: color: the line's own colour, a Framework role (which follows the theme) or a CSS colour, over --sf-chart-sparkline-color; a value that is not a colour is dropped and one under 3:1 against the background is reported in the console.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do: color defaults to empty, so a sparkline draws as before.

entries.summary: palette: the seriess' colours as a named set (vivid, soft, warm, cool, brand), each colour a light-dark pair on the Framework's tone ladder, 3:1 against surfaces 0-2 in both themes and, for the first five, told apart under the three common colour-vision deficiencies; colors still wins for the seriess it names.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do: palette defaults to theme, so a chart draws as before; set palette to use a named set.

entries.summary: sf-chart-heatmap: a measure over two categories as a grid of cells (x, y and value fields), coloured by the steps of a sequential scale (one role family) or a diverging one (two families around a neutral middle, which way is better set by better) on the theme's own tones in light and dark; the value written in each cell where it fits at 4.5:1, gaps as outlined empty cells, a legend of the scale, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor over the grid said in a live region, a summary sentence, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.
The diverging scale's middle step is the Framework's --sf-chart-midpoint (pair ui-de2b4437234a) instead of the package's own neutral-90 / neutral-25; in the dark theme it is neutral-20.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do.

entries.summary: sf-chart-funnel: the stages of a process, each a subset of the last (stage and value fields, in the data's order), as bars on a common baseline or centred, the value and the conversion (of the previous stage or of the first) beside each stage, one colour for the measure, gaps as outlined empty tracks, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor over the stages said in a live region, a summary sentence (the overall conversion, the largest loss), the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-gauge: one measured value on a fixed scale (value, min, max) as a half circle or a bar, with bands in their Framework roles' colours and names, a target mark with the distance to it, the value written in its middle in its band's colour with the band's name under it, a meter with a value text for screen readers, a summary sentence, the same data as a table (hidden by default), loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-scatter: one point per row at two measures (x and y fields), with an optional third as a bubble's area (the bubble field), series by colour and mark shape (the series field), a point's name (the point field), a least-squares trend line on request, a legend that hides series, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor that walks the points in reading order and goes up and down to the nearest point, a summary sentence with each series' relation in words and r, the same data as a table, the marks on a canvas past 2,000, loading, empty and error states.

bin: a histogram of one measure (auto, about Sturges' count on a round width, or a given width): one touching bar per interval, the count of its rows or the sum of a weight (y), by series and stacked, the axis marked at the intervals' edges, the summary with each series' median and fullest interval.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do: bin defaults to none, so a chart draws as before; set bin to draw a histogram.

entries.summary: sf-chart-box: a box plot of one measure per group (the x and y fields): the median, the quartiles (linear between the two nearest), Tukey's or full-range whiskers (whiskers) and the outliers, worked out from raw rows or given per group (stats), the mean on request (mean), series side by side in a group (series), a legend that hides series, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor over groups and series, a summary sentence with each series' highest and lowest median and widest box, the same statistics as a table, loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-radar: a spoke per measure (the x field, the first straight up, then clockwise), each series a ring through its values (y fields or the series field) on one scale from min to max, the scale's rings as polygons or circles (grid), a light fill (fill), marks of their own shape per series, a gap that breaks the ring, a legend that hides series, a tooltip with every series on a spoke, a keyboard cursor round the spokes and across the series, a summary sentence with each series' strongest and weakest spoke and the first two compared, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-candlestick: the open, high, low and close of each period (x, open, high, low and close fields) on a price axis, the periods side by side in time order with the axis marked at calendar periods, a rising body hollow and a falling one filled in the success and error tones (colors {up, down}), candles or bars (shape), neighbours merged as a longer period past one per 3 px, a key of rise and fall, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor over the candles, a summary sentence with the change, the extremes and the count of rises and falls, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-waterfall: how a start value becomes an end value through steps (x and y fields), a change floating from the running total to the new one and a total row (the total field) standing on zero, a closing total added (end), thin lines joining the bars, each bar's value written with its sign (value-labels), the success, error and neutral tones (colors {up, down, total}), a key, a tooltip with the change and the total, a keyboard cursor over the steps, a summary sentence with the start, the end, the steps that added and took away most, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

entries.consumer: Nothing to do: a page's format words read as before; a page may now write decimal-<n> with two digits.
entries.summary: chart-core/format.js formats numbers and dates through the core's SF.format (core.runtime 1.20.0, pair ui-c3015f76bcc2), which took its number words from this file; the chart keeps only its axis-tick and full-date forms and its argument order. decimal-<n> now reads up to 20 digits, as the core does; nothing else a chart says changes.

sf-chart-treemap: how a whole is made of parts (x and y fields), values as the areas of rectangles laid out squarified, largest first, one level or two (the group field) with a band naming each group, a group in a chart colour (--sf-chart-N fill and line, colors by group key), the part's name and value written inside where they fit (labels), a key of the groups, a tooltip with the share, a keyboard cursor over the parts and across the groups, a summary sentence with the total, the largest part and the largest group, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-timeline: tasks or states as ranges of time on rows (row, start and end fields), a row a lane with its name at the start holding one range or many, a bar from each range's start to its end on a calendar time axis, a diamond for a milestone, a status in a chart colour (the status field, --sf-chart-N, colors by status key) with its key, a tooltip with the start, the end and the length, a keyboard cursor along the rows and across them, a summary sentence with the span, the longest range and the status that takes the most time, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

entries.consumer: Nothing to do: every chart says its numbers and dates as before.
entries.summary: chart-core/format.js imports the core's number and date formatting from its modules without side effects (core/js/format-number.js and format-date.js, core.runtime 1.28.0, pair ui-62b1d9b6dc8d) instead of the whole format module, so a chart's bundle no longer carries the relative-date and file-size formats; the core.runtime range is now ^1.28.0.

sf-chart-sankey: quantities flowing between stages or categories (source, target and value fields, the same pair summed), nodes in columns by their longest path from where the flows start and the ends in the last column, a band from node to node as wide as its flow, the order in a column chosen so the bands cross less, a node in a chart colour (--sf-chart-N, colors by node name) and its bands in the colour's light fill, names and values beside the nodes where they fit (labels), a tooltip for a node or a band, a keyboard cursor over the nodes along the largest flows, a summary sentence with the total, the largest flow and the node where the most arrives, every flow as a row of the table, loops left out and counted, loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-sunburst: a hierarchy as rings round a centre, read from an id and a parent per row (node, parent) or from a path of names (path), a parent's value its own with its children's, the top nodes sharing the turn largest first and a child its parent's angle by its share, a ring per level outside a hole with the total, a branch in its top node's chart colour (--sf-chart-N, colors by top node name) as a light fill with a line round each arc, lighter past the first ring, names along the arcs where they fit (labels), a tooltip with the shares of the parent and the whole, a keyboard cursor round the rings and in and out of them, a summary sentence with the levels, the total, the largest branch and the largest end part, every node as a row of the table, loops of parents left out and counted, loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-map: a choropleth map, a rate or a ratio by region; the regions given by the page as GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon features (shapes, shape-key, shape-name), the package holding no map; the values joined by key (region, value); mercator, albers, equirectangular or plane projection, fitted into the plot, a map across the 180th meridian kept whole; the heatmap's stepped scale on the theme's tone ladders (scale, scheme, better, steps, middle, min, max) with a legend, a region without data as a dashed outline; names in the regions where they fit (labels), a tooltip with the value and the place, a keyboard cursor over the regions in reading order and to the nearest above or below, a summary sentence with the range, the most and the least, every region as a row of the table, rows without a region counted, loading, empty and error states.

chart-core becomes the package's shared core (package.json simai.core, ABI 1): ui-builder builds it once as its own bundle that registers its modules with SF.runtimeModule, and every chart takes them from the runtime instead of inlining them, so a page with several charts loads the core once. It keeps the modules two or more charts use (arc, colors, cursor, data, decimate, describe, format, heat, palettes, path, scale, settle, stack) and timeline, kept for the view set's Gantt chart; the twelve single-chart modules (bin, box, funnel, gauge, geo, ohlc, radar, sankey, scatter, sunburst, treemap, waterfall) move into their chart's folder. Needs core.runtime 1.38.0 or newer. Nothing a chart draws or says changes.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do for a page: the Loader fetches chart-core once through each chart rule's relation to cl-chart-core. A page needs core.runtime 1.38.0 or newer.

sf-chart-metric is retired into SIMAI Framework's metric tile sf-tile-metric (decision C168): the element is now the tile's dated alias until 2027-01-01, a subclass of the class that defines sf-tile-metric with no drawing of its own. It draws the tile's markup and sheet (.sf-tile-metric-*, not .sf-chart-metric-*): money whole by default, the change as a tonal badge, the status as an icon with its word. The former data-state, the event sf-chart-metric-open (now with detail {id}) and three public variables are mapped; -label-color, -positive-color, -negative-color and -meter-color are no longer read. The rule relates cl-tile-metric instead of cl-chart-core and cl-progress-bar. No new feature lands here.
entries.consumer: Write <sf-tile-metric> where you wrote <sf-chart-metric> (Larena: its metric tile is sf-tile-metric of the Framework); the settings keep their names; put an sf-chart-sparkline in slot="chart" for the series. data-state="loading" is loading; listen for sf-tile-metric-open; style --sf-tile-metric-* instead of --sf-chart-metric-*. Markup with sf-chart-metric keeps working until 2027-01-01, drawn by the tile; selectors or tests that read .sf-chart-metric-* classes must read .sf-tile-metric-* now.

entries.summary: chart-core gains cues.js: one detection of cue mode (forced-colors: active, or a display-settings scheme on the root, by the Framework's own scheme names when its runtime has SF.displaySettings) and one page watcher for it and the theme; mark shapes per series, the marks of a long line, and seven hatches as an SVG pattern and as a CSS background. colors.js gains the label-ink choice (pickInk, composite, inkLabels): a label on a fill takes the first of the theme's inks, then black or white, that holds 4.5:1 against that fill as drawn. Exports are only added: ABI 1 stays.
entries.consumer: A chart built on an older core keeps working; a chart of this release needs this core (the release ships both).

entries.summary: sf-chart-line: cue mode (docs/DECISIONS.md D20): under forced colours or a SIMAI Framework display-settings colour scheme (data-sf-scheme on the root), where hue cannot tell series apart, every series past the first is dashed and every series carries marks of its own shape (circle, square, triangle, diamond, a triangle down; about a dozen along a long line); the legend and tooltip swatch is a short line in that dash with that mark.
entries.consumer: Nothing to change in markup. Pages that test the drawn SVG under forced colours or a display-settings scheme find the new cue marks (hatch patterns, shaped marks, the --cues root class); a scheme is set by the Framework, never by the chart.

entries.summary: sf-chart-bar (and its histogram): cue mode (docs/DECISIONS.md D20): under forced colours or a SIMAI Framework display-settings colour scheme (data-sf-scheme on the root), where hue cannot tell series apart, the bars of every series past the first have a hatch of their own (an SVG pattern of the ground's colour over the series colour), the legend swatch shows the same hatch, and a series in lines takes its dash. In forced colours the hatches replace the dashed outlines.
entries.consumer: Nothing to change in markup. Pages that test the drawn SVG under forced colours or a display-settings scheme find the new cue marks (hatch patterns, shaped marks, the --cues root class); a scheme is set by the Framework, never by the chart.

entries.summary: sf-chart-pie: cue mode (docs/DECISIONS.md D20): under forced colours or a SIMAI Framework display-settings colour scheme (data-sf-scheme on the root), where hue cannot tell series apart, every slice past the first has a hatch of its own and its legend swatch the same; the lighter second round of tones is dropped there. A share written on a slice now takes its ink against its own slice as drawn (4.5:1 in both themes and every scheme; it was 1:1 on some slices in a scheme and 3.85-4.49:1 on lighter slices in the site theme), with a ring of the slice colour in cue mode so the hatch never crosses its letters.
entries.consumer: Nothing to change in markup. A share's ink is now written in its style after each render; a page that set the share colour through .sf-chart-pie-share CSS loses that rule to the chosen ink.

entries.summary: sf-chart-parts: cue mode (docs/DECISIONS.md D20): under forced colours or a SIMAI Framework display-settings colour scheme (data-sf-scheme on the root), where hue cannot tell series apart, every part past the first has a hatch of its own (a CSS background of the ground's colour over the part colour) and its list swatch the same; the lighter second round of tones is dropped there; the free remainder stays the plain track.
entries.consumer: Nothing to change in markup. Pages that test the drawn SVG under forced colours or a display-settings scheme find the new cue marks (hatch patterns, shaped marks, the --cues root class); a scheme is set by the Framework, never by the chart.

entries.summary: sf-chart-box: cue mode (docs/DECISIONS.md D20): under forced colours or a SIMAI Framework display-settings colour scheme (data-sf-scheme on the root), where hue cannot tell series apart, a series past the first has its box's dash outside forced colours too (it had it in forced colours only).
entries.consumer: Nothing to change in markup. Pages that test the drawn SVG under forced colours or a display-settings scheme find the new cue marks (hatch patterns, shaped marks, the --cues root class); a scheme is set by the Framework, never by the chart.

entries.summary: sf-chart-scatter: cue mode (docs/DECISIONS.md D20): under forced colours or a SIMAI Framework display-settings colour scheme (data-sf-scheme on the root), where hue cannot tell series apart, points keep their shapes, and bubbles, all circles, take their series' dash outside forced colours too.
entries.consumer: Nothing to change in markup. Pages that test the drawn SVG under forced colours or a display-settings scheme find the new cue marks (hatch patterns, shaped marks, the --cues root class); a scheme is set by the Framework, never by the chart.

entries.summary: sf-chart-radar: cue mode (docs/DECISIONS.md D20): under forced colours or a SIMAI Framework display-settings colour scheme (data-sf-scheme on the root), where hue cannot tell series apart, the marks keep their shapes, and a ring past the first takes its dash outside forced colours too.

entries.summary: sf-chart-waterfall: cue mode (docs/DECISIONS.md D20): under forced colours or a SIMAI Framework display-settings colour scheme (data-sf-scheme on the root), where hue cannot tell series apart, the success and error tones become one tone, so a rise is drawn hollow and a total dashed, as in forced colours.
